pages.title: Adjectives and colors
rules: The color goes BEFORE the noun: a red car.
Colors do not change in the plural: two red cars.
With be, the color goes AFTER: The car is red.
examples: De que cor é sua bolsa?

pages.head: Rosa's toy shop
text: Rosa has a toy shop with colorful things. In the window there is a red car, a blue ball and a green frog. On the shelf there is a yellow duck, a white rabbit and a black cat.
A boy named Ben comes in with his mother. "What's your favorite color?" asks Rosa. "Blue!" says Ben. Rosa gives him the blue ball. "It's a present," she says. Ben is very happy.
Lily loves purple. She chooses a purple teddy bear. "My favorite color is purple, too," says Rosa. Now Lily has a purple bear and a big smile.
tf: There is a red car in the window.
Rosa gives Ben a blue ball.
pages.talk: What is the color of your favorite toy or object?

pages.title: Colors: fact file
text: Colors are in many English expressions: 'feeling blue' = sad; 'green with envy' = jealous; 'in the red' = losing money; 'a white lie' = a small, harmless lie.
In traffic lights: red = stop, yellow = get ready, green = go.
A rainbow has 7 colors: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo and violet.
qs: How many colors has a rainbow?

pages.title: My favorite things
pages.task: Write about your favorite things and their colors (6 sentences).
pages.tip: Use: My favorite color is … I have a … (color + noun). The … is … (be + color).

model.title: Model
text: [I have] a blue bag and [a red] pen.
[The sky is] blue [and the sun is] yellow.

check: I used color + noun (a red pen).
I used be + color (The sky is blue).

pages.homework: Find 10 objects at home and write their color in English. Take a photo of your 'rainbow' of things!
